title: Zoom Google Calendar Integration: How to Set It Up
summary: Zoom google calendar integration allows users to sync meeting links and attendee lists automatically across platforms to streamline scheduling tasks.
body_markdown:
## Troubleshooting common Zoom and Google Calendar sync errors


Mismatched permission scopes or expired credentials are the typical culprits for API failures in meeting synchronizations, rather than logic errors in the workflow.


Identifying the specific error code returned by the endpoint allows you to pinpoint whether the failure occurred at the identity provider level or within the application’s rate-limiting tier.


The 401 Unauthorized error means the Zoom access token has expired or was revoked, meaning the automation can't act on behalf of the user.


The 403 Forbidden error indicates the Google Calendar API request lacks the necessary OAuth scopes, so the application is blocked from writing to the specific primary calendar.


Rate Limit Exceeded means the workflow has hit the threshold of **10,000 requests per 100 seconds** , which causes the request to fail and return an HTTP 429 error rather than a temporary lockout.


Meeting ID Not Found occurs when the event was manually deleted in the Zoom web portal, so the calendar sync is attempting to update a resource that doesn't exist.


Correcting these issues ensures that meeting links and participant lists remain consistent across both platforms without manual intervention.


### Resolving '403 forbidden' errors in Google Calendar


A '403 Forbidden' error indicates that the authenticated account doesn't have the "Manage" permission level required to modify calendar events.


While a connection might succeed for reading data, writing a Zoom link into the event description requires the` https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events` scope to be explicitly granted during the initial OAuth handshake.


If you're using a Google Workspace service account, the domain administrator must also enable domain-wide delegation. This allows the automation to impersonate the specific user who owns the calendar.


### Fixing Zoom JWT and OAuth authentication failures


Authentication failures occur when the app credentials in the Zoom App Marketplace don't match the environment variables in your integration.


Zoom has deprecated standalone JWT (JSON Web Token) apps in favor of Server-to-Server OAuth, which requires a specific Account ID, Client ID, and Client Secret to generate short-lived tokens.


If the workflow fails with a "401 Unauthorized" message, the refresh token has likely been invalidated by a password change or a manual deauthorization in the marketplace settings. This requires a re-authentication to establish a new secure session.


### Fixing Zoom and Google Calendar time zone mismatches


Meetings often appear several hours off because Google Calendar and[Zoom](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/we-now-have-more-than-1000-apps-on-the-zoom-app-marketplace/) handle UTC offsets differently. Google Calendar defaults to the time zone set in the user's primary calendar settings. Zoom meetings are created based on the time zone of the API user's profile.


To prevent scheduling conflicts, you must pass the` start_time` in ISO 8601 format with a clear offset. You can also use a reasoning model like[Gemini](https://gemini.google/subscriptions) 3.8 Flash to normalize the incoming timestamps into a single standard before the data reaches the destination app.


### Syncing recurring meetings


Targeting the specific` instanceId` of a Google Calendar event rather than the` recurringEventId` of the parent series allows you to sync recurring meetings accurately.


Mapping to the parent ID only updates the template for the series, which causes individual exceptions (like a holiday reschedule) to revert to the wrong time. The following logic ensures that updates to a single occurrence in a series correctly update the corresponding Zoom session:


The parent recurring event icon in Google Calendar is linked to multiple instance icons, with a Custom API Call block fetching the specific Instance ID for the Zoom update.


This granular targeting prevents the "series drift" where a change to one Monday meeting accidentally overwrites the settings for every Monday for the rest of the year.


By using the Google Calendar API` instances` endpoint, you isolate the specific Unix timestamp of the occurrence you intend to modify.


### How do I prevent private calendar events from creating Zoom links?


A conditional filter must evaluate the` visibility` property of the Google Calendar event object before the data reaches the Zoom API.


If the` visibility` field is set to` private` or` confidential` , the workflow must terminate immediately to ensure sensitive appointment titles or attendee lists aren't logged in the Zoom dashboard.


Filtering at the logic layer is more reliable than relying on user behavior. It removes the risk of a person forgetting to uncheck a "Make it Zoom" box on a personal doctor's appointment.


### Does this integration work with Zoom Webinars?


By swapping the standard` /meetings` endpoint for the` /webinars` endpoint in the API request configuration, this integration works with Zoom Webinars.


Because Zoom treats Webinars as a distinct object type with different metadata requirements, such as panelist permissions and registration toggles, a standard meeting sync will fail with a 404 error.


Zoom Webinars require a` webinar_id` and support unique registration URLs for each attendee.


Zoom Meetings require a` meeting_id` and typically use a static join link for all participants. Switching between these two modes allows you to use a single Google Calendar to manage both internal team syncs and large-scale public broadcasts without maintaining separate scheduling tools.
